blocks.text: . MARATHA CONFEDERACY (1720 - 1818)
Born at: Shivneri Fort in 1630.
Religious teacher: Samarth Ramdas.
Early Conquests & Military Tactics
At the young age of 16, Shivaji captured the Torana Fort (first victory) and renamed it Prachandagad (meaning 'Massive Fort').

Shivaji mastered the art of Guerrilla Warfare (known as Ganimi Kava). He used the rugged terrain of the Sahyadri mountains to launch surprise attacks and defeat much larger Mughal armies. Ghode Modni: A folk dance of Goa celebrating Maratha victory Expeditions of Shivaji Battle of Pratapgarh (1659)
The battle was fought between the Maratha forces led by Shivaji and the Bijapur troops under General Afzal Khan, (representing Adil Shah) to crush Shivaji's rising power.
Shivaji defeated Afzal Khan through brilliant counter-strategy Shivaji killing Afzal called Wagh Nagh marking the Khan using Wagh Nagh Marathas' first major victory.
Conflict with Shaista Khan (1660 — 1663)

Shaista Khan (Governor of Deccan) was deputed by Aurangzeb to put down rising power of Shivaji in 1660 (Shivaji lost Poona but later made a bold attack against him in 1663 and plundered Surat (1664) and later Ahmadnagar).
Treaty of Purandar (1665)

In 1665 AD, Aurangzeb appointed Raja Jai Singh I of Amber to lead a campaign against Shivaji, resulting in Raigad Fort the Treaty of Purandar. Shivaji agreed to give his 23 out of total 35 Forts to Mughals.
Agra Visit & Escape (1666 AD): Shivaji visited Aurangzeb's court in Agra but was insulted and imprisoned.
He famously escaped later that year (legend says by hiding in a basket of sweets).
Battle of Salher (1672)
Maratha forces led by Shivaji (commanded by Prataprao Gujar and Moropant Pingle) defeated Mughal army.
In 1674 AD, Shivaji proclaimed himself "Chhatrapati" at his coronation ceremony held at Raigad Fort.
The Ashtapradhan System (Council of 8 Ministers):
1. Peshwa: Prime Minister (Head of Administration).
2. Amatya: Finance Minister (Managed Treasury).
3. Mantri (Waqia-Navis): Interior Minister (Intelligence/ Home).
4. Sachiv (Shurunavis): Secretary (Drafted Royal Orders).
5. Sumant: Foreign Minister (Diplomacy).
6. Senapati: Commander-in-Chief (Military Campaigns).
7. Panditrao: High Priest (Religious Affairs).
8. Nyayadhyaksha: Chief Justice (Judicial Matters).
Shivaji introduced Marathi in place of Persian and coined Sanskrit technical terms for administrative purposes.
Literary Texts language which Maratha Revenue Sources used: Modi Script
The Marathas collected specific taxes from territories outside their direct control(Swarajya).
Chauth:
Meaning: "One-Fourth" (1/4th).
Rate: 25% of the land revenue.
Purpose: It was a protection tax. Territories paid this to avoid Maratha raids.
Sardeshmukhi: An additional 10% tax imposed on top of Chauth.
Purpose: Collected in areas where Marathas claimed hereditary rights (Sardeshmukh) or where their troops were stationed.

Balaji Viswanath (1713-1720)
In 1713, he became the first Peshwa (PM of Marathas).
He began his career as small revenue official and was given the title "Senakarte" (Maker of the Army) by Shahu in 1708.
The Peshwaship became a hereditary position from his reign.
He was the eldest son of Balaji Viswanath.
He defeated: Nizam-ul-Mulk or Asaf Jah I (Khan Siddiqi, the first Nizam of Hyderabad).
He signed: Treaty of Doraha Sarai with Jai Singh after a victory over a combined force of the Nizam, Awadh, and Rajput states of Jaipur and Kota.
In 1737, he raided Delhi.

Balaji Baji Rao (1740-1761)
He is also known as Nana Saheb.

During his tenure, the 3rd Battle of Panipat was fought between Marathas and Afghans in 1761. Peshwa Sadashivrao Bhau led the Maratha army and Ahmad Shah Abdali from Durrani Empire, led the Afghan forces. The Marathas lost the battle (One of the deadliest battles).

1st Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782)
This was started due to an internal conflict. Raghunath Rao, brother of Balaji Baji Rao wanted to become Peshwa.
However, Nana Fadnavis (Finance Minister) didn't want him to become Peshwa.
This war began when Raghunath Rao signed the Treaty of Surat (1775) and later the Treaty of Purandar (1776) with the British to gain support to become Peshwa.
The Britishers were defeated initially and Treaty of Wadgaon (1779) was signed.
Subsequently, Britishers attacked again under the leadership of Warren Hastings and defeated Marathas.
Treaty of Salbai (1782) was signed at the end.
2nd Anglo Maratha War (1803-1805)
British Leadership:
Deccan: Led by Arthur Wellesley.
North India: Led by General Lake.
Baji Rao II signed a subsidiary alliance with the British in the form of Treaty of Bassein (1802) which led to the 2nd Anglo-Maratha War. This war was won by British.
The 2nd Anglo-Maratha War ended with signing of Treaty of Rajghat (1805) with Holkars.
+ The Treaty of Deogaon signed after Battle of Argaon during 2nd Anglo-Maratha War (1803) with Bhonsles Dynasty. Cuttack was acquired by Britishers after this war.
3rd Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818)
This war is often regarded as "Pindari War'.
Pindaris were tribal people that supported Marathas during raids.
Baji Rao IJ was captured and sent to Bithoor (Kanpur).
Treaty of Mandsaur (1818) signed between the British and the Holkar chief.
From 1818, Peshwaship was abolished.
The Maratha Military Landscapes of India were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2025 as India's 44th World Heritage Site.
